newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-U.S. TAKES FIVE GOLDS, RILEY TOPS HEYNS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-U.S. TAKES FIVE GOLDS, RILEY TOPS HEYNS.

text.p: The United States swept five of the eight golds at stake in the Pan Pacific championships on Monday while Australia took the other three including an emotional win by breaststroker Samantha Riley.

All of the winning times were the fastest in the world this year, including the quickest by a U.S. team in the 4x200 metres freestyle relay since 1988 and the sixth fastest time ever in the men's 100 breaststroke.
The relay team of Chad Carvin, Thomas Malchow, Taner Ugur and Josh Davis won in seven minutes 13.99 seconds, the quickest since the Matt Biondi-anchored team won the Seoul Olympics in 7:12.51.
American Kurt Grote took the 100 breaststroke in 1:01.22 and said his times will only get better ahead of the Sydney Olympics in 2000.
"I'm not thinking about records as much as gold medals in Sydney," he said.
Riley swam away from South Africa's world-record holder and Olympic gold medalist Penny Heyns to win the women's 100 breaststroke in 1:07.81.
Heyns finished in 1:08.65. Riley said the win helped wipe away the pain caused by the accusations made against her for testing positive in a doping test late in 1995 after she took a headache pill.
Although she was eventually cleared, Riley did not recover her form in time for the Olympics and finished third in the 100 race which Heyns won and out of the medals in the 200 breaststroke.
"It does feel great," Riley said after her win. "Last year wasn't the greatest for me."
The United States might have won six golds but lost 400 individual medley world record holder and Olympic champion Tom Dolan to an asthma attack in the heats.

Australian Matthew Dunn overtook Canadian Curtis Myden in the last 20 metres to win in 4:16.11. Myden finished in 4:16.30. Dolan, who holds the world record of 4:12.30, was leading his heat when he suffered the attack.
American Ron Karnaugh, at 31 the oldest competitor in Fukuoka, finished fifth in the race.

The third Australian gold went to Michael Klim, who broke the Australian and Commonwealth record he set in the morning heats to win the men's 100 freestyle in 49.46. His time in the preliminaries was 49.52.
Klim, who turns 20 on Wednesday, caught American Neil Walker (49.57) in the last 10 metres to win.
American five-times Olympic gold medalist Jenny Thompson held off hard-charging Le Jingyi of China to win the women's 100 freestyle in 54.82.
Le, the world-recordholder and Olympic champion in the event, finished in 54.86 after putting on a late surge to draw close to Thompson.
"I'm really excited about beating her," Thompson said. "She's the world champion and it's always good racing against her."
Thompson also anchored the U.S. to victory in the women's 4x200 freestyle relay in 8:07.82, earning her 15th gold medal in five Pan Pacific appearances.
The other U.S. gold went to Kristine Quance who finished ahead of teammate Madeline Crippen in the women's 400 individual medley in a time of 4:39.61.
About 300 swimmers are competing in the meet, part of the leadup to January's world championships in Perth.
